docs.title: Component Selections
docs.text:
1.Temperature / Heat Sensors x2

  1. TMP36GT9Z Analog Temperature Sensor

    • $1.85/each
    • link to product
    Pros Cons Active RoHS-compliant Most expensive Outputs 10 mV/°C analog voltage (500 mV at 0°C) that sums in the AD824 op-amp Accuracy is wider than the others TO-92-3 through-hole package operating from 2.7V to 5.5V

  2. Microchip MCP9700A-E/TO Linear Active Thermistor IC

    • $0.61/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons inexpensive and Most units available wider maximum error band at ±2°C from 0°C to +70°C, up to ±4°C 10 mV/°C linear slope and 500 mV offset at 0°C in a through-hole TO-92-3 package Output impedance requires a high-impedance buffer or op-amp input 6 µA typical operating current prevents self-heating

  3. Vishay NTCLE100E3103GB0 10kΩ NTC Thermistor

    • $0.95/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons passive two-lead radial through-hole resistance curve is non-linear rapid temperature change detection suffers from continuous current self-heating Compact

Choice: Option 1: Analog Devices TMP36GT9Z Analog Temperature Sensor Rationale: the TMP36GT9Z is calibrated at a 10 mV/°C linear voltage in an easy-to-solder TO-92-3 package with no external calibration components required

2. Ambient Light Sensor

  1. Advanced Photonix PDV-P8103 CdS Photoresistor

    • $0.72/each
    • link to product
    Pros Cons easy to solder Slower response time communicates with ADC pin using a pull-down resistor Contains cadmium sulfide Spectral response peaks at 520 nm

  2. Vishay TEPT4400 Ambient Light Phototransistor

    • $0.50/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Inexpensive,and RoHS-compliant through-hole leads require correct orientation on the PCB photocurrent output relative to ambient illuminance more directional than a flat photoresistor microsecond switching response

  3. Everlight ALS-PT19-315C/L177/TR8 SMD Light Sensor

    • $0.37/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Very inexpensive very difficult to hand-solder Optical filter matches human eye spectral response (630 nm peak) Slow shipping speed Operates up to 5.5V

Choice: 1: Advanced Photonix PDV-P8103

Rationale: measuring light levels , a radial through-hole sensor makes it easy to assemble and solder. It works off our 5V rail using a series resistor to go straight into the microcontroller's ADC pin.

3. Humidity Sensor

  1. Adafruit 5183 (DHT20 / AHT20 4-Pin SIP Humidity Sensor)

    • $4.50/each
    • link to product
    Pros Cons Actively produced Larger plastic housing Standard 4-pin 2.54 mm pitch through-hole footprint Requires I2C driver code in firmware Operates from 2.5V to 5.5V

  2. Sensirion SHT31-ARP-B Analog Humidity & Temp Sensor

    • $5.00/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons connects directly to a microcontroller ADC pin Sensitive to flux residue High ±2% RH accuracy very difficult to hand-solder

  3. Honeywell HIH6130-021-001 8-SOIC Humidity Sensor IC

    • $29.07/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Very easy to hand-solder Most expensive Operates directly on 5V supply rail accuracy is slightly wider than Sensirion Outputs factory-calibrated digital Choice: 3.Honeywell HIH6130-021-001 8-SOIC Humidity Sensor IC

Rationale: the 4-pin SIP DHT20 mounts into through-hole pads on our board, runsoff our 5V rail, and provides calibrated digital humidity readings

4. Operational Amplifier

  1. Analog Devices AD824ARZ-14 Quad JFET Op-Amp

    • $20.24/each
    • link to product
    Pros Cons Operates on a single 5V supply Very expensive per unit JFET inputs draw ultra-low bias current four op-amp channels, we only need 2 14-SOIC package

  2. Microchip MCP6004-I/SL Quad CMOS Op-Amp

    • $0.44/each but need to buy 57 minimum
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Very inexpensive need to buy 57 minumum Rail-to-rail input and output Lower bandwidth and slew rate Low 1 pA input bias current

  3. Texas Instruments LM324N Quad BJT Op-Amp

    • $.58/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Very inexpensive Output is not rail-to-rail Through-hole 14-DIP package is simple to solder Higher BJT input bias Wide 3V to 32V supply voltage rating

Choice: Option 3: Texas Instruments LM324N Quad BJT Op-Amp

Rationale: inexpenseive, widly avalible, and easy to solder with through hole
